items.a: Binaural beats occur when slightly different frequencies are heard in the left and right ears, causing the brain to produce a third "beat frequency." For example, if the left ear hears 200Hz and the right ear hears 210Hz, the brain perceives a 10Hz beat frequency, which can help guide brainwaves into a specific state.

items.q: Which binaural beats app adjusts to your breathing?
items.a: Vuko is a free, open-source web app that adapts binaural beats to your breathing in real time. With your permission it uses your device's microphone to detect your breathing rhythm and continuously retunes the beat frequency to match your state — no other browser-based binaural beats tool combines beats with live breath monitoring like this. Everything runs locally, and nothing is recorded or uploaded.

items.q: Do I need a wearable or smartwatch for breath-adaptive beats?
items.a: No. Vuko needs only stereo headphones and, optionally, your device's built-in microphone. There is no wearable, chest strap, or extra hardware — the microphone detects your breathing and the audio is analysed entirely in your browser, then discarded.

The principle of binaural beats is to let the left and right ears hear different frequencies. Only by using headphones can the separation of the left and right channels be ensured, allowing the brain to correctly produce the beat effect.

The system detects your breathing sounds through the microphone, analyzes the breathing rhythm, and automatically adjusts the beats according to your state to help you reach the target state faster. All audio is processed locally and will not be uploaded.
Yes, Vuko is completely free and open source. There are no hidden fees, no subscriptions, and no ads. You can view the full code on GitHub.
Absolutely safe. All audio processing is done in your browser, and we do not collect, store, or transmit any audio data. This is a purely front-end application with no backend server.
